metadata.description: Testosterone decline evidence paired with TFR data for countries with longitudinal T-studies

studies.authors: Travison TG, Araujo AB, O'Donnell AB, Kupelian V, McKinlay JB
studies.title: A population-level decline in serum testosterone levels in American men
studies.finding: Age-independent secular decline in total and bioavailable testosterone
studies.bermInterpretation: Direct pathway captured (BMI-adjusted); mediated pathway removed by adjustment

studies.authors: Mazur A, Westerman R, Mueller U
studies.title: Is rising obesity causing a secular (age-independent) decline in testosterone levels?
studies.bmiNote: Natural control: weight-stable men lost 117 ng/dL (19%) over 20 years
studies.finding: Weight-stable US Air Force veterans showed secular T decline, excluding obesity as sufficient explanation
studies.bermInterpretation: Smoking gun for direct pathway (~67%); weight-stable subgroup eliminates mediated pathway naturally

studies.authors: Perheentupa A, Makinen J, Laatikainen T, Vierula M, Skakkebaek NE, Andersson AM, Toppari J
studies.title: A cohort effect on serum testosterone levels in Finnish men
studies.finding: 37% cohort-specific T decline; LH and FSH also declined in later cohorts
studies.bermInterpretation: Rosetta stone: Finland early electrification -> early T decline -> TFR collapse after 2010 (threshold crossed ~2018)

studies.authors: Chodick G, Epstein S, Shalev V
studies.title: Secular trends in testosterone -- findings from a large state-mandate care provider
studies.finding: Largest single-country study: unlikely that rising obesity is sufficient to account for the declining T
studies.bermInterpretation: Total effect (direct + mediated); Israel high cultural TFR masks biological decline

studies.authors: Andersson AM, Jensen TK, Juul A, Petersen JH, Jorgensen T, Skakkebaek NE
studies.title: Secular decline in male testosterone and sex hormone binding globulin serum levels in Danish population surveys
studies.bermInterpretation: Mediated pathway dominates in this population -- BMI adjustment removes the dominant signal (overcorrection)

studies.authors: Nyante SJ, Graubard BI, Li Y, McQuillan GM, Platz EA, Rohrmann S, Bradwin G, McGlynn KA
studies.title: Trends in sex hormone concentrations in US males: 1988-1991 to 1999-2004
studies.bmiNote: No decline detected; may reflect assay method change + mediation removal
studies.finding: No secular decline observed in NHANES data
studies.bermInterpretation: Assay method transition + mediation pathway removal -> signal obscured; not a contradiction

studies.authors: Santi D, Spaggiari G, Cason K, Simoni M
studies.title: Secular decline of testosterone and sex hormone-binding globulin serum levels: a systematic review and meta-analysis
studies.finding: Both T AND LH decline independent of age, BMI, and assay method -- HPG axis resetting
studies.bermInterpretation: Confirms multi-pathway model: Pathway A (direct Leydig Cav3.2->StAR) + HPG-level disruption. LH decline rules out simple feedback compensation

studies.title: Secular trends in testosterone among Korean men
studies.finding: Testosterone decline in Korean male population
studies.bermInterpretation: Highest EMF density country -> fastest T decline -> lowest TFR (0.72), consistent with dose-response

causal_decomposition.mediatedMechanism: EMF -> 6 metabolic pathways -> BMI increase -> aromatase/SHBG -> T decline
causal_decomposition.caveat: These proportions are approximate, derived from Mazur 2013 dichotomized weight groups. Formal mediation analysis (SEM) may yield different results.
